title: Scrofula as a named lymph-node TB
dek: An old word for tuberculous cervical lymphadenitis. Useful as a search alias. Not a separate pathogen and not a king's-touch protocol.
story: Scrofula is Wikipedia's historical name for tuberculous cervical lymphadenitis ('king's evil' in older English). The organism is still MTBC. The specimen is still a node. The NAAT is still a WRD if you obtain tissue or an aspirate correctly.
Nontuberculous mycobacteria cause a pediatric lymphadenitis that can mimic the same word. That is why the NTM plate sits in related[] — the English name is older than the speciation.
Do not treat a Wikipedia etymology as a reason to skip HIV testing, chest imaging, or microbiology. Cervical nodes are a site, not a syndrome that ends the work-up.
deep: BCG lymphadenitis in an infant is a different epidemiologic object that can share the neck.
Fistulae and scrofuloderma are cutaneous extensions; they are still TB disease.
Fine-needle aspiration versus excision is a surgical/ID judgement, not an encyclopedia dose.
RIF status still comes from Ultra/culture/WGS, not from the Old English.

visual.caption: The word scrofula forks into MTBC node disease, NTM node disease, and BCG adenitis. The word does not choose the fork.
